rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening verse introduces the sūrah, with its explanation developed here and further elaborated later.
rows.anchor: This verse forms the introduction of this sūrah. It is has been explained here in detail and more details are coming up ahead

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling God’s beneficence in revelation, the verse turns to His power and oneness.
rows.anchor: In the earlier verse, God has referred to His beneficence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is sovereign, the Qur’an is the universe’s kingly directive and rejection invites a revenge no one can prevent.
rows.anchor: It is the directive of the real king of this universe that has to be obeyed come what may

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has neither children nor partners and needs no helper to own His kingdom.
rows.anchor: Neither does He have a son nor a daughter nor any partner in His sovereignty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation’s appointed measures prove oneness: lifespans, clouds, winds, sun, and moon all remain within limits set by their wise creator.
rows.anchor: By their very existence, they bear witness that they have been created by a powerful and wise God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adversaries’ denial of the Qur’an on the basis of imaginary, powerless partners is extreme foolishness.
rows.anchor: they have set up such feeble partners with God

rows.speaker: Quraysh
rows.claim: Quraysh conceded the Qur’an’s eloquence and force but tried to make people deny its divine origin, calling it Muhammad’s fabrication.
rows.anchor: They were forced to acknowledge this feature. However, they wanted to dispel the notion of its divinity among the masses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vague charge that others helped Muhammad arose because the Qur’an gives detailed, accurate accounts of earlier messengers; the vagueness avoids exposing a false accusation by naming someone.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, it was but appropriate to keep the blame vague

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s propaganda implied that educated People of the Book or foreigners supplied material that Muhammad then attributed to an angel.
rows.anchor: some educated individuals from the People of the Book or other nations have become the Prophet’s companions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic verb means to perpetrate, while ẓulm denotes the preceding polytheism and zur the Quraysh’s allegation; the verse’s silence foreshadows their fate.
rows.anchor: means “to perpetrate.” This usage is common in Arabic

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can mean that the stories are dictated to Muhammad or delivered to him in writing; the written-form meaning is intended because Quraysh knew he was unlettered.
rows.anchor: it can mean both “they are dictated to him,” as well as “they are imparted to him in written form.” Here the second of these meanings is implied

rows.speaker: Quraysh
rows.claim: Quraysh claimed that the Book was a mixture of past-prophet stories and falsehood, written for Muhammad and delivered morning and evening, to deny its wisdom and divine origin.
rows.anchor: It is in fact made up of anecdotes of past prophets and nations intertwined with truth and falsehood

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allegation fails the Qur’an’s challenge: Quraysh had ample Arab, non-Arab, and scriptural expertise but could not produce a comparable book.
rows.anchor: had thousands of Arabs and non-Arabs and People of the Book at their disposal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an needs no Arab or foreign helper: every line shows the revealer’s knowledge of the universe, its history, present duties, and future outcomes.
rows.anchor: cited lessons of the past, explained responsibilities of the present

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy explains why revelation gives people room to repent instead of immediate punishment, though the consequence of rejection remains certain.
rows.anchor: since He is merciful, He is not in haste to do so

rows.speaker: disbelievers
rows.claim: They mock a human messenger and demand an angel, treasure, or orchard as proof of his status.
rows.anchor: why did He send a human being like them? He has a whole army of angels

rows.speaker: disbelievers
rows.claim: They tell believers that Muhammad has lost his senses under a magic spell.
rows.anchor: They are following someone who has lost his senses since a spell of magic has been weaved upon him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats 17:48; the expression about parables can also mean raising an objection or making sarcastic remarks.
rows.anchor: it also means to raise an objection on someone or to be pass sarcastic remarks on

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person enslaved to desire exceeds natural limits and becomes worse than an animal.
rows.anchor: he crosses all limits of his instincts and nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts from historical accounts that assured the Prophet to physical-world signs that reinforce their arguments and equip him to preach conclusively through the Qur’an despite opponents’ demands.
rows.anchor: attention is directed to signs found in the physical world around human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should persist with the Qur’an’s proof and disregard objections raised to harass him or bolster opponents’ standing.
rows.anchor: They do this to merely harass him or to strengthen their own reputation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question addresses each person and refers to the shadow God spreads over the world.
rows.anchor: address every person individually and refer to the shadow of the night

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone can spread and withdraw the night’s shadow, an alternation essential to life; the sun gradually removes darkness and can replace the night if God wills.
rows.anchor: Both this spreading and drawing away are essential to maintain life in this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a guide makes things visible, the sun guides people out of night’s darkness; without its light they would wander without a way.
rows.anchor: the sun becomes guide in the darkness of night. It does away with it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daytime rising recalls resurrection after death, and the word nushur eloquently points to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: they will also one day awake from the sleep of death on the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day display providence, mercy, power, wisdom, monotheism, and the hereafter; they prove Qur’anic claims to those willing to reflect, a theme revisited in 25:82-87.
rows.anchor: All these signs are sufficient to prove every statement of the Qur’ ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here rahmah means rain: although it does not fall daily, every earthly living being depends on it, and rain displays God’s attributes on which the Qur’an’s message rests.
rows.anchor: The word  ﺔٌ رَﺣۡﻤَ connotes rain here, and it has been used in this connotation at a number of instances in the Qur’ ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain’s harmony with the needs of creatures points to a wise creator rather than accident or conflicting forces, imposes responsibility, and recalls God’s power to resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: Can it be imagined after observing the harmony between diverse elements of nature that conflicting intentions control it?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Many” qualifies humans and animals because some creatures do not need water; the two named groups are prominent land creatures that subsume the rest.
rows.anchor: The adjective “many” qualifies animals and human beings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the command to explain “it” refers to the Qur’an, whose earlier arguments support its message; repeated explanations have conveyed truth to every group, yet most reject it stubbornly.
rows.anchor: it is these people who are entirely at fault

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have sent a warner to every settlement if Muhammad’s solitary preaching effort were insufficient, but the fault lies with people who close their eyes and abandon reason.
rows.anchor: had the Almighty seen that the task of preaching was falling short because the Prophet (sws) was alone in this task

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should ignore demands meant to pester him and wage major jihad through the Qur’an, completing proof and leaving receptive people an opportunity and no excuse before God.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) wage jihād through this Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ṭāʿah means listening to someone and giving that person regard.
rows.anchor: to listen to someone and giving regard to him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maraja means “to leave,” ʿadhb means very sweet and tasty, and ḥijran maḥjūra refers to a strong obstruction, as in the earlier discussion of 25:22; its construction resembles 4:57.
rows.anchor: The word ﻣَﺮَجَ means “to leave,” and ﻋَﺬۡبٌ means “very sweet and tasty.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden barrier between fresh and salt waters shows that opposing forces in nature are controlled by God and cannot exceed their limits; polytheists wrongly treated such forces as independent deities.
rows.anchor: these opposing forces are not independent and authoritative; they are in fact under the control of an all powerful being

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates humans and mates from water, then creates blood and marriage ties that form families and societies; producing opposites and joining them harmoniously shows one wise power governs the universe.
rows.anchor: only God has the power to create opposites from water and then knit them into a single thread through His power and wisdom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the preceding signs drawn from the world around people, this argument comes from within them.
rows.anchor: the earlier arguments were drawn from the world around human beings, while this one has been drawn from within them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs within and around people show a single peerless creator and ruler, yet people worship powerless things and become rivals of their Lord.
rows.anchor: The signs found around human beings and those within them point to the fact that this universe has a single master and creator who is peerless
